approach: Split the v-t graph into six straight segments, use the signed area under each for displacement, and the sum of the unsigned areas for distance.

steps.text: Find the signed area of each of the six straight segments of the graph, since area under a v-t graph gives displacement.
Add the six signed areas for the total displacement, then divide by the total time for the average velocity.
Add the magnitudes of the six areas for the total distance travelled, then divide by the total time for the average speed.
steps.why_this_step: Average speed uses distance travelled, not net displacement, so the sign of each area is dropped before adding.

final_answer.value: (a) average velocity = 50/7 m/s ≈ 7.14 m/s, (b) average speed = 10 m/s

common_mistakes.text: Dividing the total distance 140 m by 14 s and calling it the average velocity gives 10 m/s, which is actually the average speed.
Dividing the net displacement 100 m by 14 s and calling it the average speed gives 50/7 m/s, which is actually the average velocity.
